_description: Pillar 2 — Tagging (per-pillar rule model). Loaded by pre-write-guard.sh at runtime. Homes R-05 (deny, tag-validation), R-47 (advisory, tag-presence), R-50 (advisory, 25-tag cap). The R-60 (deny, tag grammar) _rules[] OBJECT is homed in governance/naming-rules.json — it appears in the tagging rule_id_range (category=tagging) only, NOT duplicated here. _rules[] is the per-pillar rule SoT (each object carries home/category/surface?/status). Carries the canonical tag-prefix taxonomy. Tags are the user-side query surface (Obsidian graph view, filter pane, MOC patterns); frontmatter fields are the Claude-side substrate.

_design_notes.consumer: pre-write-guard.sh — tag-validation branch (R-05) + tag-presence advisory (R-47); librarian tag-coverage-audit (R-47, R-50); onboarder consolidation prompt (R-50, install-time)
_design_notes.lockstep_pair: System Governance - Tagging.md (narrative spoke) + hooks/pre-write-guard.sh (tag-validation branch) + governance/log-subtype-registry.json (system-utility canonicality discipline)
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 documentary lockstep — tagging-rules.json + System Governance - Tagging.md narrative spoke + pre-write-guard.sh tag-validation branch move in one commit (the r37_coupled_surfaces set declared at governance/_index.json#pillars[tagging]). NO write-time DENY for R-37, by design (R-37 is documentary across the governance surface — git commit-boundary atomicity + librarian governance-parity-audit at session-close; a PreToolUse hook sees exactly one file per call and cannot inspect a multi-file commit set).
_design_notes.rule_id_range_reconciliation: _index.json#pillars[tagging].rule_id_range = [R-05, R-60, R-47, R-50]. This pillar's _rules[] = [R-05, R-47, R-50] (3 objects). R-60 is in the range (its tag-grammar substance is category=tagging) but its _rules[] object is HOMED in governance/naming-rules.json. This is the home != range divergence — the tagging surface owns R-60's runtime substance (it validates against this pillar's taxonomy); naming owns R-60's declaration site.

taxonomy._description: Faceted tag taxonomy (canonical authority). Foundation user_facing_dimensions ship [] empty — concrete user-facing dimensions belong to adopter overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes + .user_facing_dimensions, populated by onboarding archetype seeds at install time. Foundation ships taxonomy SHAPE + system-utility dimensions (status, log) governed by log-subtype-registry. Runtime allowlist = foundation + overlay-master union.
taxonomy.canonical_authority: governance/tagging-rules.json#taxonomy (the dissolved-schema anchors _tag_prefixes / _tag_prefixes_meta resolve to dimension_prefixes / (system_utility_dimensions + user_facing_dimensions + cap_25_applies_to) here)
taxonomy.system_utility_governance: log-subtype-registry (canonical values per dimension; near-match DENY via R-05)
taxonomy._runtime_allowlist_resolution: Hook union-resolve over foundation-master.tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes + overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes — foundation-master.json composes the runtime view from this pillar; the adopter overlay extends it.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh tag-validation branch (system-utility dimension DENY on near-match)
_rules.failure_mode: Near-match drift in system-utility dimensions fragments operational subtypes within weeks. Two runs of the same routine emit two different tag values (e.g., #log/backlog-hygiene vs #log/backlog-cleanup), and the user-side graph filter splits routine activity across variant spellings. The discipline restores stability: every routine activity uses the STABLE, canonical tag value registered at first emission, and the hook DENIES near-match drift.
_rules.rule_text: Tags within system-utility dimensions (#log/*, #status/*) must match a value registered in governance/log-subtype-registry.json. Near-match writes (Levenshtein distance <= 2 or substring containment of an existing canonical value) are DENIED with a 'did you mean #<dim>/<canonical>?' suggestion. Genuinely new subtypes register explicitly via the prompt-and-commit pattern at first emission. The discipline mirrors the canonical-tag-per-concept principle on the system-utility surface where LLM stochasticity would otherwise fragment the vocabulary.

_rules.failure_mode: Non-exempt files written without tags become orphans in Obsidian graph view — invisible to user-side queries even though the file is legible to Claude-side surfaces via frontmatter fields. Pre-write tag-presence advisory surfaces the omission at the moment of write rather than at the weekly audit, closing a ~7-day detection lag.
_rules.rule_text: Every non-exempt vault write MUST carry a non-empty `tags:` array in its frontmatter. Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory ([R-47 TAG PRESENCE]) when the field is missing or empty (tags: []). Distinguishes 'missing' (no tags: line) vs 'empty' (line present, no items). Exempt paths are enumerated in this rule's `r47_exempt_paths` array — they cover archive surfaces, ideation-brief symlinks, machine-emitted scratch/build zones, and system infrastructure paths whose tag-absence is structurally legitimate. The librarian tag-coverage-audit walks the vault at audit time and surfaces longer-running orphans + near-miss patterns (#scope/decisions vs #scope/decision — one is likely a typo) as advisory findings the operator triages.
_rules.exempt_path_semantics: positive-list — unenumerated top-level paths default to the advisory firing (NOT auto-exempt). Adding a new exempt path requires R-37 documentary lockstep updating this rule + pre-write-guard.sh + the narrative spoke (System Governance - Tagging.md) + foundation-master.json bundle composition (composed via tools/build-foundation-master.sh, never hand-edited).
_rules.seed_taxonomy_exempt_paths_semantics: DEDICATED tag-TAXONOMY exempt-list — SEPARATE from r47_exempt_paths (which is the tag-PRESENCE exempt-list for R-47). The foundation ships its vault-init seed surface tagged with adopter-tier dimensions (#scope/reference on the six System Governance/*.md spokes, #system-governance on System Governance/_index.md, #vault-writers on Vault Writers/_index.md) that model good tagging for adopters; the foundation taxonomy itself ships user_facing_dimensions:[] BY DESIGN (taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions), so those seed tags are NOT members of the foundation allowlist and the tag-taxonomy membership arm flags them as 9 day-one violations. These two glob surfaces exempt EXACTLY those seeds from the tag-not-in-taxonomy membership check ONLY — seeds stay byte-unchanged, still obey the R-47 tag-PRESENCE rule (r47_exempt_paths untouched), and adopter-authored tags on non-exempt paths are unaffected. Composed deterministically to foundation-master.json#seed_taxonomy_exempt_paths_composed via tools/build-foundation-master.sh (never hand-edit the bundle). Forward note: _load_tag_prefixes() reads only FM_FOUNDATION_MASTER and does not yet union the adopter overlay-master taxonomy — until that union-read lands, exemption (not adopter-dimension-registration) is the correct minimum-viable closure.

enforcement_layer: librarian tag-coverage-audit (audit-time consolidation prompt at 80% threshold)
_rules.source: governance/tagging-rules.json :: _rules (SoT; 25-tag cap grounded in Forte/Dubois working-vocabulary research + Hedden faceted-classification literature + Adobe AEM and SharePoint enterprise CMS picklist patterns)
_rules.failure_mode: Cap-widening defeats the working-memory rationale silently. An adopter activates a new engagement, user-facing tag count approaches 25, and the path of least resistance is 'raise the cap to 30.' Past 25, decision fatigue produces variant-creation rather than canonical-term selection, the vocabulary fragments, and user-side recall collapses. The cap is structural, not aspirational — silent widening is rejected; deliberate Layer 3 override is supported with audit trail.
_rules.rule_text: Total count of distinct values across user-facing dimensions (declared at runtime by union of foundation-master.tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions + overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions) MUST stay under 25. System-utility dimensions (log, status) are exempt — they are machine-emitted and governed by the log-subtype registry (R-05). The librarian tag-coverage-audit emits an advisory when user-facing usage approaches 80% of the cap (>= 20 active values), surfaces a consolidation prompt with retire-candidate recommendations, and requires deliberate Layer 3 override (`overlay-master.json :: tagging_cap_override` with rationale + audit-trail entry) before silent widening can proceed.
_rules.override_mechanism: Layer 3 overlay-master.json :: tagging_cap_override with rationale + audit-trail entry
